assert abs(cohen_d([2,3,4],[1,2,3])+1)<1e-10, 'Swapping groups reverses the sign'

title: Compute discriminator AUC with ties
prompt: Implement auc(human_scores,bot_scores): larger means more likely bot. Compare every bot-human pair, giving 1 for bot higher, 0.5 for equal, 0 for lower; average. Reject either empty group. Example humans [0.2,0.5], bots [0.5,0.8] gives 0.875.
tests:
assert auc([0.2,0.5],[0.5,0.8])==0.875, 'Tied pairs receive half credit'
assert auc([1,1],[1,1])==0.5, 'All ties give chance ranking'
assert auc([0,0],[1,1])==1, 'Perfect separation gives AUC one'
assert auc([1,1],[0,0])==0, 'Reversed scores give AUC zero'
try: auc([],[1])
except ValueError: pass
else: assert False, 'Both classes need observations'
hint: Use nested loops and divide by the product of group sizes.

title: Build a human-versus-human null
prompt: Complete human_null(values,repeats,seed). values is a finite 2-D NumPy matrix with an even number of match rows (at least four), one column per feature. Use one default_rng. Each repeat permutes whole rows, splits into equal halves, computes supplied cohen_d per column, and returns their RMS. Return a list of repeat scores. Example repeats=3 returns three nonnegative scores; the same seed reproduces them.
tests:
values=np.array([[0.,1.],[1.,2.],[2.,4.],[3.,8.],[4.,16.],[5.,32.]])
s=human_null(values,5,19)
assert len(s)==5 and all(np.isfinite(v) and v>=0 for v in s), 'Return one finite RMS per split'
assert s==human_null(values,5,19), 'A fixed seed must reproduce the human control'
rng=np.random.default_rng(19);expected=[]
for _ in range(5):
    idx=rng.permutation(6);a=values[idx[:3]];b=values[idx[3:]]
    scale=np.sqrt((a.var(axis=0,ddof=1)+b.var(axis=0,ddof=1))/2)
    d=(b.mean(axis=0)-a.mean(axis=0))/scale
    expected.append(float(np.sqrt((d*d).mean())))
assert np.allclose(s,expected), 'Permute whole rows and use all feature columns'
assert human_null(values,0,19)==[], 'Zero repeats requests no scores'
hint: Use one row-index permutation per repeat for all columns, then np.sqrt(np.mean(effects**2)).
